title.zh: 卷四十九 列傳第四十三 文學上
title.raw: 卷四十九 列傳第四十三 文學上 Volume 49: Men of Letters 1

sentences.zh: 到沆 丘遲 劉苞 袁峻 庾於陵 弟肩吾 劉昭 何遜 鍾嶸 周興嗣 吳均

translations.literal: Dao Hang, Qiu Chi, Liu Bao, Yuan Jun, Yu Yuling, younger brother Jianwu, Liu Zhao, He Xun, Zhong Rong, Zhou Xingsi, Wu Jun
translations.idiomatic: Dao Hang · Qiu Chi · Liu Bao · Yuan Jun · Yu Yuling · Jianwu (brother) · Liu Zhao · He Xun · Zhong Rong · Zhou Xingsi · Wu Jun

sentences.zh: 昔司馬遷、班固書，並爲《司馬相如傳》，相如不預漢廷大事，蓋取其文章尤著也。

translations.literal: In the past Sima Qian and Ban Gu in their histories both made a "Biography of Sima Xiangru"; Xiangru did not take part in great affairs of the Han court—they took him because his writings were especially outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Sima Qian and Ban Gu each wrote a Sima Xiangru biography though Xiangru never shaped Han statecraft—they chose him for supreme literary fame.

sentences.zh: 固又爲《賈鄒枚路傳》，亦取其能文傳焉。

translations.literal: Gu also wrote the "Biographies of Jia, Zou, Mei, and Lu," likewise taking them because they could write and be transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Gu also wrote the Jia–Zou–Mei–Lu group biography, again honoring men who wrote well enough to endure.

sentences.zh: 范氏《後漢書》有《文苑傳》，所載之人，其詳已甚。

translations.literal: Fan Ye's Book of the Later Han has a "Garden of Letters," and those it records are already treated at great length.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ye's Later Han includes a Garden of Letters with very full notices already.

sentences.zh: 然經禮樂而緯國家，通古今而述美惡，非文莫可也。

translations.literal: Yet to weave the state through rites and music and to link past and present in telling good and evil—nothing but writing will serve.
translations.idiomatic: Yet binding statecraft to rites and music and threading ages to judge good and evil demands writing alone.

sentences.zh: 是以君臨天下者，莫不敦悅其義，縉紳之學，咸貴尚其道，古往今來，未之能易。

translations.literal: Hence rulers over all under Heaven have none who did not esteem and delight in its meaning; gentry learning all prized and honored its Way—from antiquity to the present it has not been changed.
translations.idiomatic: So every sovereign has cherished its doctrine; every scholar-official has honored its path—unchanged through time.

sentences.zh: 高祖聰明文思，光宅區宇，旁求儒雅，詔采異人，文章之盛，煥乎俱集。

translations.literal: Gaozu was wise and brilliant in literary thought, his light dwelling over the realm; he sought Confucian elegance on every side and issued edicts to gather unusual men—the splendor of letters gathered all together.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, clear-minded and literary, lit the realm, sought Confucians everywhere, and summoned odd talents until letters blazed in one place.

sentences.zh: 每所御幸，輒命羣臣賦詩，其文善者，賜以金帛，詣闕庭而獻賦頌者，或引見焉。

translations.literal: On each tour he would order the ministers to compose poems; those whose writing was good received gold and silk, and those who came to the court with fu and eulogies were sometimes granted audience.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he traveled he made ministers write poems; the best won gold and silk, and some who brought fu and hymns to court were received in audience.

sentences.zh: 其在位者，則沈約、江淹、任昉，並以文采，妙絕當時。

translations.literal: Among those in office were Shen Yue, Jiang Yan, and Ren Fang—all famed for literary color, unsurpassed in their day.
translations.idiomatic: At court Shen Yue, Jiang Yan, and Ren Fang led in literary brilliance, unmatched then.

sentences.zh: 至若彭城到沆、吳興丘遲、東海王僧孺、吳郡張率等，或入直文德，通讌壽光，皆後來之選也。

translations.literal: As for Pengcheng Dao Hang, Wuxing Qiu Chi, Donghai Wang Sengru, Wu commandery Zhang Shuai, and the like—some entered duty at Wende, some passed feasts at Shouguang—all were choices of the next generation.
translations.idiomatic: Pengcheng's Dao Hang, Wuxing's Qiu Chi, Donghai's Wang Sengru, Wu's Zhang Shuai, and others served at Wende or Shouguang feasts—rising stars all.

sentences.zh: 約、淹、昉、僧孺，率別以功跡論。

translations.literal: Yue, Yan, Fang, and Sengru are treated separately under deeds of merit.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, Yan, Fang, and Sengru appear elsewhere for their achievements.

sentences.zh: 今綴到沆等文兼學者，至太清中人，爲《文學傳》云。

translations.literal: Now I join Dao Hang and other men of letters and learning down to men of the Taiping era in this "Biography of Men of Letters."
translations.idiomatic: Here I collect Dao Hang and fellow writers and scholars through the Taiping period in this Biography of Men of Letters.

sentences.zh: 到沆字茂瀣，彭城武原人也。

translations.literal: Dao Hang, courtesy name Maoxie, was a man of Wuyuan in Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Hang, styled Maoxie, came from Wuyuan in Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 曾祖彥之，宋將軍。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yanzhi was a Song general.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yanzhi served Song as a general.

sentences.zh: 父撝，齊五兵尚書。

translations.literal: His father Hui was Qi Minister of the Five Arms.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui was Qi minister of the five arms.

sentences.zh: 沆幼聰敏，五歲時，撝於屏風抄古詩，沆請教讀一遍，便能諷誦，無所遺失。

translations.literal: Hang was clever as a child; at five, when Hui copied ancient poems on a screen, Hang asked to be taught, read them once, and could chant them by heart with nothing lost.
translations.idiomatic: At five Hang heard his father copy poems on a screen, asked to learn them, read once, and recited every line from memory.

sentences.zh: 旣長勤學，善屬文，工篆隸。

translations.literal: When grown he studied diligently, was skilled at writing, and excelled in seal and clerical scripts.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he studied hard, wrote well, and mastered seal and clerical script.

sentences.zh: 美風神，容止可悅。

translations.literal: His bearing was handsome and his deportment pleasing.
translations.idiomatic: He had fine presence and pleasing manners.

sentences.zh: 齊建武中，起家後軍法曹參軍。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu era of Qi he first took office as Army Adjutant in the Rear Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi Jianwu he began as Rear Guard army adjutant.

sentences.zh: 天監初，遷征虜主簿。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianjian he was promoted to chief clerk of the Expeditionary Force.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tianjian he became chief clerk of the expeditionary force.

sentences.zh: 高祖初臨天下，收拔賢俊，甚愛其才。

translations.literal: When Gaozu first held the realm he gathered the worthy and greatly loved Hang's talent.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, newly ruling, sought talent and prized Hang highly.

sentences.zh: 東宮建，以爲太子洗馬。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Palace was established he was made Crown Prince's Libationer.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was named he became the prince's libationer.

sentences.zh: 時文德殿置學士省，召高才碩學者待詔其中，使校定墳史，詔沆通籍焉。

translations.literal: At that time the Wende Hall housed a Scholars' Office, summoning men of high talent and great learning to await edicts there and collate the classics and histories; Hang was ordered to hold a pass for entry.
translations.idiomatic: Wende Hall then held a scholars' office of eminent readers collating the classics; Hang received palace access.

sentences.zh: 時高祖讌華光殿，命羣臣賦詩，獨詔沆爲二百字，三刻使成。

translations.literal: Once Gaozu feasted at Huaguang Hall and ordered the ministers to compose poems, singling out Hang alone for two hundred characters to be finished in three quarters of an hour.
translations.idiomatic: At a Huaguang feast Gaozu ordered poems but gave Hang alone two hundred characters and three quarters of an hour.

sentences.zh: 沆於坐立奏，其文甚美。

translations.literal: Hang composed while seated and presented it; the text was very fine.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote seated, presented it, and the piece was excellent.

sentences.zh: 俄以洗馬管東宮書記、散騎省優策文。

translations.literal: Soon he was libationer managing Eastern Palace records and drafting superior policy papers in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he managed Eastern Palace records and drafted superior memorials for the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔尚書郎在職清能或人才高妙者爲侍郎，以沆爲殿中曹侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year an edict made incumbent Secretariat gentlemen who were pure and able or of lofty talent into vice directors; Hang was made Vice Director of the Palace Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Year three made able Secretariat gentlemen into vice directors; Hang became vice director of the palace bureau.

sentences.zh: 沆從父兄溉、洽，並有才名，時皆相代爲殿中，當世榮之。

translations.literal: Hang's cousins Gai and Qia both had literary fame and at the time alternated in the palace bureau—an honor of the age.
translations.idiomatic: His cousins Gai and Qia, both famed writers, alternated in that bureau—a contemporary glory.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷太子中舍人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to Crown Prince Household Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Year four he rose to crown prince household attendant.

sentences.zh: 沆爲人不自伐，不論人長短，樂安任昉、南鄉范雲皆與友善。

translations.literal: Hang did not boast himself nor discuss others' faults; Ren Fang of Le'an and Fan Yun of Nanxiang were both his close friends.
translations.idiomatic: He never boasted or gossiped about others; Ren Fang and Fan Yun were close friends.

sentences.zh: 其年，遷丹陽尹丞，以疾不能處職事，遷北中郎諮議參軍。

translations.literal: That year he was made Assistant Magistrate of Danyang but, ill, could not handle duties and was moved to Consulting Colonel of the Northern Army.
translations.idiomatic: That year he became Danyang assistant magistrate, fell ill, and shifted to northern army consulting colonel.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒官，年三十。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died in office at age thirty.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth year he died in office at thirty.

sentences.zh: 高祖甚傷惜焉，詔賜錢二萬，布三十匹。

translations.literal: Gaozu deeply mourned him and ordered two ten-thousands in cash and thirty bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu mourned him and granted twenty thousand cash and thirty bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 所著詩賦百餘篇。

translations.literal: His collected poems and fu number over a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He left more than a hundred poems and fu.

sentences.zh: 丘遲字希範，吳興烏程人也。

translations.literal: Qiu Chi, courtesy name Xifan, was a man of Wucheng in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Chi, styled Xifan, was from Wucheng in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 父靈鞠，有才名，仕齊官至太中大夫。

translations.literal: His father Lingju had literary fame and served Qi to Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lingju, a noted writer, reached Qi Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 遲八歲便屬文，靈鞠常謂氣骨似我。

translations.literal: At eight Chi could compose; Lingju often said his bone and breath were like mine.
translations.idiomatic: At eight Chi wrote prose; Lingju said his spirit matched his own.

sentences.zh: 黃門郎謝超宗、徵士何點並見而異之。

translations.literal: Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Xie Chaozong and recluse He Dian both saw him and were struck.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Chaozong and He Dian both marveled at him young.

sentences.zh: 及長，州辟從事，舉秀才，除太學博士。

translations.literal: When grown he was summoned as staff aide, nominated as Outstanding Talent, and appointed Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he was a staff aide, nominated outstanding talent, and made imperial university erudite.

sentences.zh: 遷大司馬行參軍，遭父憂去職。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Army Aide in the Grand Marshal's service and left office on his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to grand marshal army aide, then left for mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除西中郎參軍。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was made Army Aide of the Western Army.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he became western army aide.

sentences.zh: 累遷殿中郎，以母憂去職。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Palace Gentleman and left on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to palace gentleman, then left for his mother's mourning.

sentences.zh: 服除，復爲殿中郎，遷車騎錄事參軍。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he again became Palace Gentleman and was promoted to Army Registrar.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he returned as palace gentleman, then army registrar.

sentences.zh: 高祖平京邑，霸府開，引爲驃騎主簿，甚被禮遇。

translations.literal: When Gaozu pacified the capital he opened the lord's office and made Chi Rapid Cavalry chief clerk, treating him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the capital he made Chi rapid cavalry chief clerk and honored him.

sentences.zh: 時勸進梁王及殊禮，皆遲文也。

translations.literal: At that time the memorials urging the King of Liang to advance and for special rites were all Chi's writing.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials urging Liang Wang to advance and for special rites were Chi's work.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐阼，拜散騎侍郎，俄遷中書侍郎，領吳興邑中正，待詔文德殿。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne Chi was made Secretariat Gentleman, soon promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat, headed the Wuxing district chief, and awaited edicts at Wende Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At enthronement Chi became secretariat gentleman, then vice director, Wuxing chief, and Wende attendant.

sentences.zh: 時高祖著《連珠》，詔羣臣繼作者數十人，遲文最美。

translations.literal: When Gaozu wrote Linked Pearls he ordered dozens of ministers to continue them; Chi's text was finest.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's Linked Pearls drew dozens of continuations; Chi's was best.

sentences.zh: 天監三年，出爲永嘉太守，在郡不稱職，爲有司所糾，高祖愛其才，寢其奏。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianjian he went out as Administrator of Yongjia; in the commandery he did not perform well and was impeached by the authorities, but Gaozu loved his talent and shelved the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjian year three he governed Yongjia poorly and was impeached; Gaozu shelved it for love of his gift.

sentences.zh: 四年，中軍將軍臨川王宏北伐，遲爲諮議參軍，領記室。

translations.literal: In the fourth year General of the Center Linchuan Wang Hong marched north; Chi was consulting colonel and chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Year four Prince Linchuan marched north; Chi was consulting colonel and chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 時陳伯之在北，與魏軍來距，遲以書喻之，伯之遂降。

translations.literal: Chen Bozhi was then in the north opposing Wei with his army; Chi wrote to persuade him, and Bozhi surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Bozhi held the north against Wei; Chi's letter persuaded him to surrender.

sentences.zh: 還拜中書郎，遷司徒從事中郎。

translations.literal: On return he was made Secretariat Gentleman and promoted to Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Returning he became secretariat gentleman, then secretariat attendant.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒官，時年四十五。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died in office at age forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh year he died in office at forty-five.

sentences.zh: 所著詩賦行於世。

translations.literal: His poems and fu circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His poems and fu circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 劉苞字孝嘗，彭城人也。

translations.literal: Liu Bao, courtesy name Xiaochang, was a man of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bao, styled Xiaochang, was from Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 祖勔，宋司空。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xun was Song Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Xun had been Song Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 父愃，齊太子中庶子。

translations.literal: His father Xuan was Qi Crown Prince Household Vice-Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xuan was Qi crown prince vice-supervisor.

sentences.zh: 苞四歲而父終，及年六七歲，見諸父常泣。

translations.literal: Bao's father died when he was four; at six or seven he wept whenever he saw his uncles.
translations.idiomatic: His father died when he was four; at six or seven he wept at sight of his uncles.

sentences.zh: 時伯、叔父悛、繪等並顯貴，苞母謂其畏憚，怒之。

translations.literal: His uncles Juan and Hui and others were then all eminent; his mother thought he feared them and was angry.
translations.idiomatic: His uncles Juan, Hui, and others were eminent; his mother thought fear made him weep and scolded him.

sentences.zh: 苞對曰：「早孤不及有識，聞諸父多相似，故心中欲悲，無有佗意。

translations.literal: Bao replied: "Orphaned early, I never knew them; hearing that my uncles greatly resemble one another, my heart simply wants to grieve—there is no other intent.
translations.idiomatic: Bao answered: "Orphaned young I never knew them; told my uncles are much alike, I grieve from the heart only—no other motive.

sentences.zh: 」因而歔欷，母亦慟甚。

translations.literal: "; and he sobbed; his mother too was deeply stricken.
translations.idiomatic: "; he sobbed, and his mother wept bitterly too.

sentences.zh: 初，苞父母及兩兄相繼亡沒，悉假瘞焉。

translations.literal: Earlier Bao's parents and two elder brothers had died in succession and were all given temporary burial.
translations.idiomatic: Parents and two elder brothers had died in turn and lain in temporary graves.

sentences.zh: 苞年十六，始移墓所，經營改葬，不資諸父，未幾皆畢，繪常嘆服之。

translations.literal: At sixteen Bao moved the graves and arranged reburial without help from his uncles; soon all was done—Hui often sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he moved and reburied them without uncles' aid; Hui marveled when all was finished.

sentences.zh: 少好學，能屬文。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and could write.
translations.idiomatic: Young he loved learning and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 起家爲司徒法曹行參軍，不就。

translations.literal: He first took office as Army Aide in the Secretariat but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered secretariat army aide but declined.

sentences.zh: 天監初，以臨川王妃弟故，自征虜主簿仍遷王中軍功曹，累遷尚書庫部侍郎、丹陽尹丞、太子太傅丞、尚書殿中侍郎、南徐州治中，以公事免。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianjian, as younger brother of the Linchuan princess, he went from chief clerk of the expeditionary force to merit officer of the prince's center army, then rose through posts in the treasury, Danyang, crown prince tutor, palace bureau, and southern Xuzhou staff, and was dismissed for public business.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tianjian, as the Linchuan princess's brother, he rose from expeditionary clerk through treasury, Danyang, tutor, palace, and Xuzhou posts until dismissed on public grounds.

sentences.zh: 久之，爲太子洗馬，掌書記，侍講壽光殿。

translations.literal: After long service he was Crown Prince Libationer, kept records, and lectured at Shouguang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was crown prince libationer, kept records, and lectured at Shouguang.

sentences.zh: 自高祖卽位，引後進文學之士，苞及從兄孝綽、從弟孺、同郡到溉、溉弟洽、從弟沆、吳郡陸倕、張率並以文藻見知，多預讌坐，雖仕進有前後，其賞賜不殊。

translations.literal: From Gaozu's accession he drew later literary men; Bao with his cousin Xiaochuo, cousin Ru, fellow townsman Dao Gai, Gai's brother Qia, cousin Hang, Lu Chun of Wu, and Zhang Shuai were all known for ornament and often at feasts—though promotions differed, rewards did not.
translations.idiomatic: Since Gaozu's accession Bao, Xiaochuo, Ru, Dao Gai, Qia, Hang, Lu Chun, and Zhang Shuai shone at court feasts; ranks differed but gifts did not.

sentences.zh: 天監十年，卒，時年三十。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tianjian he died at age thirty.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjian year ten he died at thirty.

sentences.zh: 臨終，呼友人南陽劉之遴託以喪事，務從儉率。

translations.literal: At the end he called his friend Liu Zhilin of Nanyang to entrust funeral matters, insisting on thrift.
translations.idiomatic: Dying he asked Liu Zhilin to bury him thriftily.

sentences.zh: 苞居官有能名，性和而直，與人交，面折其非，退稱其美，情無所隱，士友咸以此嘆惜之。

translations.literal: In office Bao had a name for ability; his nature was gentle yet straight—with friends he rebuked their faults to their faces but praised their virtues in private, hiding nothing; gentlemen lamented this.
translations.idiomatic: Able in office, gentle yet frank, he criticized friends openly and praised them privately; all mourned that honesty.

sentences.zh: 袁峻字孝高，陳郡陽夏人，魏郎中令渙之八世孫也。

translations.literal: Yuan Jun, courtesy name Xiaogao, was from Yangxia in Chen commandery, eighth-generation descendant of Wei Palace Attendant Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jun, styled Xiaogao, of Chen Yangxia, eighth generation from Wei's Yuan Huan.

sentences.zh: 峻早孤，篤志好學，家貧無書，每從人假借，必皆抄寫，自課日五十紙，紙數不登，則不休息。

translations.literal: Jun was orphaned early, devoted in will and fond of learning; the family was poor and had no books—whenever he borrowed he copied everything, setting himself fifty sheets a day and not resting if the count fell short.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, poor, bookless, he copied every loan at fifty sheets a day and would not rest short of quota.

sentences.zh: 訥言語，工文辭。

translations.literal: He was slow of speech and skilled in literary phrasing.
translations.idiomatic: Slow-spoken, he excelled in literary phrasing.

sentences.zh: 義師剋京邑，鄱陽王恢東鎮破岡，峻隨王知管記事。

translations.literal: When the righteous army took the capital, Prince of Poyang Hui marched east to Pogang; Jun followed the prince managing records.
translations.idiomatic: When the army took the capital Jun followed Prince Poyang Hui east and kept his records.

sentences.zh: 天監初，鄱陽國建，以峻爲侍郎，從鎮京口。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianjian the Poyang state was founded and Jun was made Vice Director, following the prince to garrison Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tianjian he became Poyang vice director and followed the prince to Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 王遷郢州，兼都曹參軍。

translations.literal: When the prince moved to Yingzhou he also served as Army Registrar.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince went to Yingzhou he was army registrar too.

sentences.zh: 高祖雅好辭賦，時獻文於南闕者相望焉，其藻麗可觀，或見賞擢。

translations.literal: Gaozu loved ci and fu; at that time those presenting writing at the Southern Gate were unbroken, and the ornate were sometimes rewarded and promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu loved fu; writers thronged the southern gate and the ornate sometimes won office.

sentences.zh: 六年，峻乃擬揚雄《官箴》奏之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Jun modeled Yang Xiong's "Admonition on Offices" and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Year six he modeled Yang Xiong's Admonition on Offices and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉焉，賜束帛。

translations.literal: Gaozu was pleased and gave silk.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu praised him and gave silk.

sentences.zh: 除員外散騎侍郎，直文德學士省，抄《史記》、《漢書》各爲二十卷。

translations.literal: He was made Supernumerary Secretariat Gentleman, served in the Wende scholars' office, and copied the Records of the Historian and Book of Han, twenty scrolls each.
translations.idiomatic: He became supernumerary secretariat gentleman, served Wende scholars, and copied Records and Han, twenty scrolls each.

sentences.zh: 又奉敕與陸倕各制《新闕銘》，辭多不載。

translations.literal: He was also ordered with Lu Chun each to compose a New Palace Inscription; most of the text is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered with Lu Chun to write New Palace inscriptions—most text omitted here.

sentences.zh: 庾於陵字子介，散騎常侍黔婁之弟也。

translations.literal: Yu Yuling, courtesy name Zijie, was younger brother of Secretariat Regular Attendant Qianlou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yuling, styled Zijie, was younger brother of Regular Attendant Qianlou.

sentences.zh: 七歲能言玄理。

translations.literal: At seven he could discourse on dark learning.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he could expound dark learning.

sentences.zh: 旣長，清警博學有才思。

translations.literal: When grown he was clear, alert, broadly learned, and full of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he was clear, alert, learned, and inventive.

sentences.zh: 齊隨王子隆爲荊州，召爲主簿，使與謝朓、宗夬抄撰羣書。

translations.literal: When Qi Prince of Sui Zilong was in Jingzhou he summoned him as chief clerk and had him collate books with Xie Tiao and Zong Que.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Prince Sui in Jingzhou made him chief clerk to collate books with Xie Tiao and Zong Que.

sentences.zh: 子隆代還，又以爲送故主簿。

translations.literal: When Zilong returned to the capital he was again made chief clerk for the farewell party.
translations.idiomatic: When Zilong returned he again led the farewell staff.

sentences.zh: 子隆尋爲明帝所害，僚吏畏避，莫有至者，唯於陵與夬獨留，經理喪事。

translations.literal: Zilong was soon killed by Mingdi; staff feared and fled—only Yuling and Que stayed to manage the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi soon killed Zilong; staff fled—only Yuling and Que arranged the funeral.

sentences.zh: 始安王遙光爲撫軍，引爲行參軍，兼記室。

translations.literal: Prince of Shian Yaoguang was General Who Pacifies the Army and made him Army Aide and chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shian Yaoguang made him army aide and chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 永元末，除東陽遂安令，爲民吏所稱。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongyuan he was made Magistrate of Sui'an in Dongyang and was praised by people and officials.
translations.idiomatic: Late Yongyuan he governed Sui'an in Dongyang and won praise from people and officials.

sentences.zh: 天監初，爲建康獄平，遷尚書工部郎，待詔文德殿。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianjian he was prison reviewer in Jiankang, then promoted to Gentleman of the Ministry of Works and awaited edicts at Wende.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tianjian he reviewed Jiankang prison, then became works gentleman and Wende attendant.

sentences.zh: 出爲湘州別駕，遷驃騎錄事參軍，兼中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: He went out as Xiangzhou vice governor, then Rapid Cavalry registrar and Secretariat courier.
translations.idiomatic: He was Xiangzhou vice governor, then rapid cavalry registrar and secretariat courier.

sentences.zh: 俄領南郡邑中正，拜太子洗馬，舍人如故。

translations.literal: Soon he headed the southern district chief, was made Crown Prince Libationer, and kept his courier post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he headed the southern chief, became crown prince libationer, and kept courier duty.

sentences.zh: 舊事，東宮官屬，通爲清選，洗馬掌文翰，尤其清者。

translations.literal: By old practice Eastern Palace posts were all pure selections; the libationer held documents and was especially pure.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Palace posts were pure picks; the libationer's documents were purest of all.

sentences.zh: 近世用人，皆取甲族有才望，時於陵與周捨並擢充職，高祖曰：「官以人而清，豈限以甲族。

translations.literal: In recent times appointees were taken from great clans with talent and fame; Yuling and Zhou She were both chosen for the post, and Gaozu said: "Office is made noble by the man—why limit it to great clans?
translations.idiomatic: Lately only great clans with fame were chosen; Yuling and Zhou She were picked, and Gaozu said: "Men ennoble office—why bind it to clan?

sentences.zh: 」時論以爲美。

translations.literal: "; contemporaries praised this.
translations.idiomatic: "; the age praised it.

sentences.zh: 俄遷散騎侍郎，改領荊州大中正。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman and changed to head the Jingzhou chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was secretariat gentleman and Jingzhou chief.

sentences.zh: 累遷中書黃門侍郎，舍人、中正並如故。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat Vice Director; courier and chief posts were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to secretariat vice director while keeping courier and chief posts.

sentences.zh: 出爲宣毅晉安王長史、廣陵太守，行府州事，以公事免。

translations.literal: He went out as Chief of Staff to Prince Jin'an of Xuanyi and Administrator of Guangling, acting for the prefecture, and was dismissed on public business.
translations.idiomatic: He was Jin'an prince chief of staff and Guangling governor, acting prefecture, then dismissed.

sentences.zh: 復起爲通直郎，尋除鴻臚卿，復領荊州大中正。

translations.literal: He was reappointed Palace Attendant, soon made Minister of Ceremonies, and again headed Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Reappointed palace attendant, soon minister of ceremonies and again Jingzhou chief.

sentences.zh: 卒官，時年四十八。

translations.literal: He died in office at age forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 文集十卷。

translations.literal: His collected works were ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 弟肩吾。

translations.literal: Younger brother Jianwu.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jianwu.

sentences.zh: 肩吾字子慎。

translations.literal: Jianwu, courtesy name Zishen.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu, styled Zishen.

sentences.zh: 八歲能賦詩，特爲兄於陵所友愛。

translations.literal: At eight he could compose poetry and was especially loved by his elder brother Yuling.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he wrote verse and was Yuling's favorite brother.

sentences.zh: 初爲晉安王國常侍，仍遷王宣惠府行參軍。

translations.literal: He first served as Regular Attendant of the Jin'an princedom, then was promoted to Army Aide of the Prince's Xuanhui office.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Jin'an regular attendant, then prince Xuanhui army aide.

sentences.zh: 自是每王徙鎮，肩吾常隨府。

translations.literal: From then on whenever the prince moved his fief Jianwu followed the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the prince moved fief Jianwu followed.

sentences.zh: 歷王府中郎、雲麾參軍，並兼記室參軍。

translations.literal: He served as princely middle attendant, Cloud Banner army aide, and chief secretary throughout.
translations.idiomatic: He was princely middle attendant, cloud-banner aide, and chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 中大通三年，王爲皇太子，兼東宮通事舍人，除安西湘東王錄事參軍，俄以本官領荊州大中正。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongdatong the prince became crown prince; Jianwu was Eastern Palace courier while also Jin'an-Xiangdong recorder, and soon headed Jingzhou as chief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongdatong year three the prince became heir; Jianwu was Eastern Palace courier and Xiangdong recorder, soon Jingzhou chief.

sentences.zh: 累遷中錄事諮議參軍、太子率更令、中庶子。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to consulting colonel of the central records, Crown Prince Commissioner for Increasing the Seasons, and Household Vice-Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to central records consulting colonel, crown prince commissioner of seasons, and household vice-supervisor.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗在籓，雅好文章士，時肩吾與東海徐摛、吳郡陸杲、彭城劉遵、劉孝儀、儀弟孝威，同被賞接。

translations.literal: When Taizong was still in the fief he loved men of letters; then Jianwu with Xu Chi of Donghai, Lu Guo of Wu, Liu Zun and Liu Xiaoyi of Pengcheng, and Xiaoyi's brother Xiaowei were all favored.
translations.idiomatic: In the fief Taizong loved writers; Jianwu, Xu Chi, Lu Guo, Liu Zun, Xiaoyi, and Xiaowei were favored.

sentences.zh: 及居東宮，又開文德省，置學士，肩吾子信、摛子陵、吳郡張長公、北地傅弘、東海鮑至等充其選。

translations.literal: When he dwelt in the Eastern Palace he again opened the Wende office and placed scholars; Jianwu's son Xin, Chi's son Ling, Zhang Changgong of Wu, Fu Hong of Beidi, and Bao Zhi of Donghai were chosen.
translations.idiomatic: As crown prince he reopened Wende scholars—Jianwu's Xin, Chi's Ling, Zhang Changgong, Fu Hong, and Bao Zhi among them.

sentences.zh: 齊永明中，文士王融、謝朓、沈約文章始用四聲，以爲新變，至是轉拘聲韻，彌尚麗靡，復逾於往時。

translations.literal: In Qi Yongming, Wang Rong, Xie Tiao, and Shen Yue first used the four tones in writing as a new change; by now sound and rhyme grew stricter and ornate beauty exceeded the past.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Yongming brought four-tone verse; now rhyme grew tighter and ornament surpassed the past.

sentences.zh: 時太子與湘東王書論之曰：

translations.literal: Then the crown prince wrote to the Prince of Xiangdong discussing it, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince then wrote Prince Xiangdong, saying:

sentences.zh: 吾輩亦無所遊賞，止事披閱，性旣好文，時復短詠。

translations.literal: We too have no diversions but to spread our scrolls; our nature loves writing and we sometimes compose short pieces.
translations.idiomatic: We have no pastime but reading; nature loves letters and we sometimes write short pieces.

sentences.zh: 雖是庸音，不能閣筆，有慚伎癢，更同故態。

translations.literal: Though it is mediocre sound, we cannot lay down the brush; ashamed of the itch for skill, we relapse into the old habit.
translations.idiomatic: Mediocre as they are, we cannot stop writing—ashamed of the itch, we fall back into old ways.

sentences.zh: 比見京師文體，懦鈍殊常，競學浮疏，急爲闡緩。

translations.literal: Lately the capital style is unusually dull and blunt; all rush to learn the floating and shallow, hastening to be lax and slow.
translations.idiomatic: Lately capital style is dull; all chase the shallow and slack.

sentences.zh: 玄冬脩夜，思所不得，旣殊比興，正背《風》、《騷》。

translations.literal: On long winter nights the mind finds nothing—utterly unlike the bixing, directly betraying the Winds and Sao.
translations.idiomatic: Winter nights yield nothing—unlike bixing, betraying the Winds and Sao.

sentences.zh: 若夫六典三禮，所施則有地；

translations.literal: As for the six canons and three rites, where they apply there is a place;
translations.idiomatic: The six canons and three rites apply only where they belong;

sentences.zh: 吉凶嘉賓，用之則有所。

translations.literal: for auspicious and inauspicious, guest and host, use has its occasion.
translations.idiomatic: luck, rites, guest and host each have their occasion.

sentences.zh: 未聞吟詠情性，反擬《內則》之篇；

translations.literal: Never have I heard of chanting feeling and nature while imitating the "Neize" chapter;
translations.idiomatic: Never heard feeling sung while imitating Neize;

sentences.zh: 操筆寫志，更摹《酒誥》之作；

translations.literal: wielding the brush to write intent while copying the "Wine Admonition";
translations.idiomatic: intent written while copying the Wine Admonition;

sentences.zh: 遲遲春日，翻學《歸藏》；

translations.literal: lingering spring days while learning the Guicang;
translations.idiomatic: spring days spent imitating Guicang;

sentences.zh: 湛湛江水，遂同《大傳》。

translations.literal: deep deep river waters, then matching the Great Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: deep waters matched to the Great Commentary.

sentences.zh: 吾旣拙於爲文，不敢輕有掎摭。

translations.literal: I am clumsy at writing and dare not lightly pick faults.
translations.idiomatic: I am a poor writer and dare not pick faults lightly.

sentences.zh: 但以當世之作，歷方古之才人，遠則揚、馬、曹、王，近則潘、陸、顏、謝，而觀其遣辭用心，了不相似。

translations.literal: But taking the works of this age and comparing their wording and intent with ancient talents far back to Yang, Sima, Cao, and Wang, or near to Pan, Lu, Yan, and Xie—they are utterly unlike.
translations.idiomatic: Yet comparing today's wording and intent with Yang, Sima, Cao, Wang, Pan, Lu, Yan, and Xie—they do not resemble at all.

sentences.zh: 若以今文爲是，則古文爲非；

translations.literal: If present writing is right, then ancient writing is wrong;
translations.idiomatic: If today is right, antiquity is wrong;

sentences.zh: 若昔賢可稱，則今體宜棄。

translations.literal: if past worthies may be praised, then present style should be cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: if the ancients deserve praise, present style should be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 俱爲盍各，則未之敢許。

translations.literal: Both sides say "each has his own"—I do not dare agree.
translations.idiomatic: Each side says "to each his own"—I cannot agree.

sentences.zh: 又時有效謝康樂、裴鴻臚文者，亦頗有惑焉。

translations.literal: Moreover there are those who imitate the writing of Xie Lingyun or Vice Minister Pei—with some delusion.
translations.idiomatic: Some imitate Xie Lingyun or Vice Minister Pei—with delusion.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 謝客吐言天拔，出於自然，時有不拘，是其糟粕；

translations.literal: Master Xie's words tower heavenward, springing from nature; occasional lapses are the dregs;
translations.idiomatic: Xie's words soar naturally; lapses are dregs;

sentences.zh: 裴氏乃是良史之才，了無篇什之美。

translations.literal: Pei was talent for a fine historian, utterly without beauty in lyric pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Pei was a historian's mind, not a poet's gift.

sentences.zh: 是爲學謝則不屆其精華，但得其冗長；

translations.literal: Thus to study Xie is not to reach his essence but only to get the long-winded;
translations.idiomatic: Study Xie and you miss essence, keep length;

sentences.zh: 師裴則蔑絕其所長，惟得其所短。

translations.literal: to take Pei as teacher is to scorn his strengths and keep only his shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: Take Pei and you scorn strengths, keep flaws.

sentences.zh: 謝故巧不可階，裴亦質不宜慕。

translations.literal: Therefore Xie's craft cannot be climbed, and Pei's plainness is not to be admired.
translations.idiomatic: Xie's craft cannot be climbed; Pei's plainness is not to be copied.

sentences.zh: 故胸馳臆斷之侶，好名忘實之類，方分肉於仁獸，逞郤克於邯鄲，入鮑忘臭，效尤致禍。

translations.literal: So companions who gallop the breast and break the diaphragm, lovers of name who forget reality, split flesh on a benevolent beast and display Xi Ke at Handan, enter the brine and forget the stink, imitate the ugly and invite disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Name-chasers split flesh on a benevolent beast, play Xi Ke at Handan, enter brine and forget stink, imitate ugliness and invite harm.

sentences.zh: 決羽謝生，豈三千之可及；

translations.literal: To break feathers before Master Xie—can three thousand be reached?
translations.idiomatic: Break feathers before Xie—can three thousand match?

sentences.zh: 伏膺裴氏，懼兩唐之不傳。

translations.literal: To bow before Pei—fearing the two Tang histories will not be transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Bow to Pei—fearing the two Tang histories will not pass down.

sentences.zh: 故玉徽金銑，反爲拙目所嗤；

translations.literal: Thus jade markings and golden flutes are mocked by clumsy eyes;
translations.idiomatic: Jade pipes are laughed at by dull eyes;

sentences.zh: 《巴人下里》，更合郢中之聽。

translations.literal: "Ba people, lower village" better suit the ear of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Ba songs and lower village better please Ying's ear.

sentences.zh: 《陽春》高而不和，妙聲絕而不尋。

translations.literal: "Yangchun" is high and unharmonized; subtle sound ends and is not sought.
translations.idiomatic: Yangchun is too high to harmonize; fine sound dies unheeded.

sentences.zh: 竟不精討錙銖，核量文質，有異《巧心》，終愧妍手。

translations.literal: They do not finely weigh ounce and scruple or measure text and substance; unlike the "Clever Heart," they end ashamed before the skilled hand.
translations.idiomatic: They never weigh ounce or scruple or text and substance; unlike the Clever Heart, they shame the skilled hand.

sentences.zh: 是以握瑜懷玉之士，瞻鄭邦而知退；

translations.literal: Thus men holding jade and cherishing gems see Zheng's state and know to withdraw;
translations.idiomatic: Men with jade see Zheng and withdraw;

sentences.zh: 章甫翠履之人，望閩鄉而歎息。

translations.literal: men in cap and green shoes look toward Min lands and sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Men in caps look to Min and sigh.

sentences.zh: 詩旣若此，筆又如之。

translations.literal: If poetry is so, the brush is likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Poetry being so, prose is the same.

sentences.zh: 徒以煙墨不言，受其驅染；

translations.literal: Only because ink does not speak is it driven and dyed;
translations.idiomatic: Ink does not speak yet drives them;

sentences.zh: 紙札無情，任其搖襞。

translations.literal: paper and bamboo slips have no feeling yet are shaken and folded.
translations.idiomatic: Paper has no feeling yet is folded at will.

sentences.zh: 甚矣哉，文之橫流，一至於此！

translations.literal: Alas! the flood of letters has come to this!
translations.idiomatic: Alas! letters have flooded to this!

sentences.zh: 至如近世謝朓、沈約之詩，任昉、陸倕之筆，斯實文章之冠冕，述作之楷模。

translations.literal: As for recent Xie Tiao and Shen Yue in poetry, Ren Fang and Lu Chun in the brush—they are truly the cap and belt of letters, models of composition.
translations.idiomatic: Recent Xie Tiao and Shen Yue in poetry, Ren Fang and Lu Chun in prose—are the cap and belt of letters.

sentences.zh: 張士簡之賦，周升逸之辯，亦成佳手，難可復遇。

translations.literal: Zhang Shijian's fu and Zhou Shengyi's disputation are also fine hands hard to meet again.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shijian's fu and Zhou Shengyi's debate are fine hands rarely seen again.

sentences.zh: 文章未墜，必有英絕；

translations.literal: Letters have not yet fallen—there must be outstanding ones;
translations.idiomatic: Letters have not fallen—outstanding ones must exist;

sentences.zh: 領袖之者，非弟而誰。

translations.literal: to lead them—who if not you, younger brother?
translations.idiomatic: to lead—who but you, brother?

sentences.zh: 每欲論之，無可與語，思言子建，一共商榷。

translations.literal: Each time I wish to discuss it there is no one to speak with; I think of Zijian to deliberate together.
translations.idiomatic: I want to discuss but have no partner; I think of you, Zijian, to judge together.

sentences.zh: 辯茲清濁，使如涇、渭；

translations.literal: Discriminate clear and muddy as Jing and Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Sort clear from muddy like Jing and Wei;

sentences.zh: 論茲月旦，類彼汝南。

translations.literal: discuss as on the first of the month, like Ru'nan.
translations.idiomatic: judge like Ru'nan on the first of the month.

sentences.zh: 朱丹旣定，雌黃有別，使夫懷鼠知慚，濫竽自恥。

translations.literal: Once cinnabar is fixed and orpiment distinguished, let the rat in the bosom know shame and the false player on the yu feel disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Once red and yellow are fixed, let frauds in the bosom feel shame.

sentences.zh: 譬斯袁紹，畏見子將；

translations.literal: Like Yuan Shao fearing to see Zi'ang;
translations.idiomatic: Like Yuan Shao fearing Zi'ang;

sentences.zh: 同彼盜牛，遙羞王烈。

translations.literal: like the cattle thief ashamed before Wang Lie from afar.
translations.idiomatic: like the cattle thief ashamed before Wang Lie.

sentences.zh: 相思不見，我勞如何。

translations.literal: "Longing and not seeing—how I toil!"
translations.idiomatic: "Longing, yet not seeing—how I toil!"

sentences.zh: 太清中，侯景寇陷京都；

translations.literal: In the Taiping era Hou Jing raided and took the capital;
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Hou Jing took the capital;

sentences.zh: 及太宗卽位，以肩吾爲度支尚書。

translations.literal: when Taizong took the throne he made Jianwu Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong reigned he made Jianwu Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時上流諸蕃，並據州拒景，景矯詔遣肩吾使江州，喻當陽公大心，大心尋舉州降賊。

translations.literal: At that time the upper streams and various princes all held provinces resisting Jing; Jing forged an edict sending Jianwu to Jiangzhou to persuade Duke Daxin of Dangyang, who soon surrendered the province to the bandit.
translations.idiomatic: Princes on the upper Yangtze resisted Jing; Jing forged an edict sending Jianwu to persuade Daxin, who surrendered Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 肩吾因逃入建昌界，久之，方得赴江陵，未幾卒。

translations.literal: Jianwu fled into Jianchang territory; after long time he reached Jiangling and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu fled into Jianchang, later reached Jiangling, and soon died.

sentences.zh: 文集行於世。

translations.literal: His collected works circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His works circulated.

sentences.zh: 劉昭字宣卿，平原高唐人，晉太尉實九世孫也。

translations.literal: Liu Zhao, courtesy name Xuanqing, was from Gaotang in Pingyuan, ninth-generation descendant of Jin Grand Marshal Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhao, styled Xuanqing, of Pingyuan Gaotang, ninth generation from Jin's Liu Shi.

sentences.zh: 祖伯龍，居父憂以孝聞，宋武帝敕皇太子諸王並往吊慰，官至少府卿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Bolong was famed for filial piety in mourning for his father; Song Wudi ordered the crown prince and princes to condole and he reached Vice Director of the Palace Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Bolong was famed for mourning filial piety; Wudi sent princes to condole; he reached vice director of the palace bureau.

sentences.zh: 父彪，齊征虜晉安王記室。

translations.literal: His father Biao was staff chief secretary to the Qi expeditionary Prince Jin'an.
translations.idiomatic: His father Biao was Qi Jin'an prince chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 昭幼清警，七歲通《老》、《莊》義。

translations.literal: Zhao in youth was clear and alert; at seven he mastered the meanings of the Laozi and Zhuangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Young Zhao was alert; at seven he mastered Laozi and Zhuangzi.

sentences.zh: 旣長，勤學善屬文，外兄江淹早相稱賞。

translations.literal: When grown he studied diligently and wrote well; his maternal uncle Jiang Yan early praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Grown he studied and wrote; uncle Jiang Yan praised him early.

sentences.zh: 天監初，起家奉朝請，累遷征北行參軍、尚書倉部郎，尋除無錫令。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianjian he first became Court Gentleman for attendance, rose to northern expedition army aide and treasury gentleman, and was made Magistrate of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tianjian he was court gentleman, northern expedition aide, treasury gentleman, then Wuxi magistrate.

sentences.zh: 曆爲宣惠豫章王、中軍臨川王記室。

translations.literal: He served as chief secretary to Princes Xuanhui of Yuzhang and Linchuan of the Center Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was chief secretary to Yuzhang Xuanhui and Linchuan center army princes.

sentences.zh: 初，昭伯父肜集衆家《晉書》注干寶《晉紀》爲四十卷，至昭又集《後漢》同異以注范曄書，世稱博悉。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhao's uncle Yin had gathered many families' Jin History with Gan Bao's Jin Annals into forty scrolls; Zhao again gathered Later Han variants to annotate Fan Ye's book—the age called him broadly versed.
translations.idiomatic: Uncle Yin had compiled Jin history; Zhao annotated Fan Ye's Later Han with variants—the age called him thorough.

sentences.zh: 遷通直郎，出爲剡令，卒官。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Attendant, went out as Magistrate of Shan, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He became palace attendant, governed Shan, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 《集注後漢》一百八十卷，《幼童傳》十卷，文集十卷。

translations.literal: Collected Annotated Later Han in one hundred eighty scrolls, Biographies of Young Children in ten scrolls, collected works in ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left Annotated Later Han in 180 scrolls, Young Children in 10, and collected works in 10.

sentences.zh: 子縚，字言明。

translations.literal: His son Chao, courtesy name Yanming.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chao, styled Yanming.

sentences.zh: 亦好學，通《三禮》。

translations.literal: He too loved learning and mastered the three rites.
translations.idiomatic: Chao loved learning and mastered the three rites.

sentences.zh: 大同中，爲尚書祠部郎，尋去職，不復仕。

translations.literal: In the Datong era he was Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites, soon left office and never served again.
translations.idiomatic: Datong era he was rites gentleman, then left and never served again.

sentences.zh: 縚弟緩，字含度，少知名。

translations.literal: Chao's younger brother Huan, courtesy name Handu, was known in youth.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Huan, styled Handu, was known young.

sentences.zh: 歷官安西湘東王記室，時西府盛集文學，緩居其首。

translations.literal: In office he was chief secretary to Prince Xiangdong of the Pacifying West; the western headquarters then gathered letters and Huan led them.
translations.idiomatic: He was Xiangdong chief secretary when the western staff brimmed with letters and he led them.

sentences.zh: 除通直郎，俄遷鎮南湘東王中錄事，復隨府江州，卒。

translations.literal: He was made Palace Attendant, soon promoted to central records of the Pacifying South Xiangdong prince, followed the headquarters to Jiangzhou, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Made palace attendant, then Xiangdong central records, followed Jiangzhou, and died.

sentences.zh: 何遜字仲言，東海郯人也。

translations.literal: He Xun, courtesy name Zhongyan, was a man of Tan in Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: He Xun, styled Zhongyan, was from Tan in Donghai.

sentences.zh: 曾祖承天，宋御史中丞。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Chengtian was Song Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandfather Chengtian was Song censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 祖翼，員外郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yi was Supernumerary Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Yi was supernumerary gentleman.

sentences.zh: 父詢，齊太尉中兵參軍。

translations.literal: His father Xun was Qi staff officer in the Grand Marshal's center army.
translations.idiomatic: Father Xun was Qi grand marshal center army staff officer.

sentences.zh: 遜八歲能賦詩，弱冠，州舉秀才。

translations.literal: At eight Xun could compose poetry; at weak adulthood the province nominated him Outstanding Talent.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he wrote poetry; at weak adulthood the province nominated him outstanding talent.

sentences.zh: 南鄉范雲見其對策，大相稱賞，因結忘年交好。

translations.literal: Fan Yun of Nanxiang saw his examination answers and greatly praised him, and they formed a friendship ignoring age.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yun saw his examination answers, praised him, and they became friends ignoring age.

sentences.zh: 自是一文一詠，雲輒嗟賞，謂所親曰：「頃觀文人，質則過儒，麗則傷俗；

translations.literal: From then on whenever one wrote a piece or a poem Yun would sigh in admiration and said to intimates: "Lately I have observed men of letters—plainness overshoots the Ru, ornament wounds the vulgar;
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Yun praised every piece and told intimates: "Writers lately are too plain for Ru or too ornate for the vulgar;

sentences.zh: 其能含清濁，中今古，見之何生矣。

translations.literal: those who can hold clarity and turbidity together and hit the mean of past and present—seeing this, what is He Sheng!"
translations.idiomatic: those who hold clear and muddy and balance past and present—seeing this, what is He Sheng!"

sentences.zh: 」沈約亦愛其文，嘗謂遜曰：「吾每讀卿詩，一日三復，猶不能已。

translations.literal: "; Shen Yue also loved his writing and once told Xun: "Whenever I read your poems I go over them three times a day and still cannot stop.
translations.idiomatic: "; Shen Yue loved him too and said: "I read your poems thrice daily and cannot stop.

sentences.zh: 」其爲名流所稱如此。

translations.literal: "; such was the praise of the famous.
translations.idiomatic: "; such was fame's praise.

sentences.zh: 天監中，起家奉朝請，遷中衛建安王水曹行參軍，兼記室。

translations.literal: In the Tianjian era he first became Court Gentleman for attendance, was promoted to water bureau army aide of Prince Jian'an of the Guard, and also chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjian era he was court gentleman, then Jian'an guard water bureau aide and chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 王愛文學之士，日與遊讌，及遷江州，遜猶掌書記。

translations.literal: The prince loved literary men and daily feasted with them; when he moved to Jiangzhou Xun still kept records.
translations.idiomatic: The prince loved writers and feasted daily; moving to Jiangzhou Xun still kept records.

sentences.zh: 還爲安西安成王參軍事，兼尚書水部郎，母憂去職。

translations.literal: On return he was staff officer to Prince Cheng of Anxi and also Gentleman of the Ministry of Works water bureau, and left on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: Returning he was Cheng of Anxi staff officer and works water gentleman, then mourned his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除仁威廬陵王記室，復隨府江州，未幾卒。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was chief secretary to Prince Luling of Renwei, again followed the headquarters to Jiangzhou, and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was Luling chief secretary, followed Jiangzhou, and soon died.

sentences.zh: 東海王僧孺集其文爲八卷。

translations.literal: Wang Sengru of Donghai collected his writing in eight scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengru collected his work in eight scrolls.

sentences.zh: 初，遜文章與劉孝綽並見重於世，世謂之「何劉」。

translations.literal: Earlier Xun's writing and Liu Xiaochuo's were both weighty in the world; people called them "He–Liu."
translations.idiomatic: Xun and Liu Xiaochuo were both famed as "He–Liu."

sentences.zh: 世祖著論論之云：「詩多而能者沈約，少而能者謝朓、何遜。」

translations.literal: Shizu wrote a treatise saying: "Many poems but able—Shen Yue; few but able—Xie Tiao, He Xun."
translations.idiomatic: Shizu wrote: "Many poems, able—Shen Yue; few, able—Xie Tiao and He Xun."

sentences.zh: 時有會稽虞騫，工爲五言詩，名與遜相埒，官至王國侍郎。

translations.literal: At the time Yu Xie of Kuaiji was skilled in pentasyllabic poetry, his name matching Xun's, and he reached Princedom Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Kuaiji's Yu Xie wrote pentasyllabic verse rivaling Xun and reached princedom vice director.

sentences.zh: 其後又有會稽孔翁歸、濟陽江避，並爲南平王大司馬府記室。

translations.literal: Later there were also Kong Wengui of Kuaiji and Jiang Bi of Jiyang, both chief secretaries to the Grand Marshal of Prince Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: Later Kuaiji's Kong Wengui and Jiyang's Jiang Bi were Nanping grand marshal chief secretaries.

sentences.zh: 翁歸亦工爲詩，避博學有思理，更注《論語》、《孝經》。

translations.literal: Wengui also wrote poetry skillfully; Bi was broadly learned with subtle reasoning and further annotated the Analects and Classic of Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: Wengui wrote verse well; Bi was learned and reannotated the Analects and Filial Classic.

sentences.zh: 二人並有文集。

translations.literal: Both had collected works.
translations.idiomatic: Both had literary collections.

sentences.zh: 鍾嶸字仲偉，潁川長社人，晉侍中雅七世孫也。

translations.literal: Zhong Rong, styled Zhongwei, was a man of Changshe in Yingchuan, seventh-generation descendant of Jin Palace Attendant Zhong Ya.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Rong, styled Zhongwei, was from Changshe in Yingchuan, a seventh-generation descendant of Jin Palace Attendant Zhong Ya.

sentences.zh: 父蹈，齊中軍參軍。

translations.literal: His father Tao served Qi as Staff Officer to the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tao was a Central Army staff officer under Qi.

sentences.zh: 嶸與兄岏、弟嶼並好學，有思理。

translations.literal: Rong and his elder brother Wan and younger brother Yu all loved learning and had thoughtful minds.
translations.idiomatic: Rong, his elder brother Wan, and younger brother Yu all loved study and thought deeply.

sentences.zh: 嶸，齊永明中爲國子生，明《周易》，衛軍王儉領祭酒，頗賞接之。

translations.literal: Rong, in Qi's Yongming era, was a National University student, versed in the Book of Changes; Defender-General Wang Jian headed the Directorate and greatly favored him.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi's Yongming reign Rong studied at the National University and mastered the Changes; Wang Jian as Defender-General and Directorate head greatly favored him.

sentences.zh: 舉本州秀才。

translations.literal: He was recommended as the commandery's Outstanding Talent.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery recommended him as Outstanding Talent.

sentences.zh: 起家王國侍郎，遷撫軍行參軍，出爲安國令。

translations.literal: He began office as Gentleman of the princely establishment, was promoted to Staff Officer on the Pacification Army's staff, and went out as magistrate of An'guo.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a princely Gentleman, became Pacification Army staff officer, then magistrate of An'guo.

sentences.zh: 永元末，除司徒行參軍。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yongyuan era he was appointed Staff Officer on the Secretariat's staff.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongyuan's end he joined the Secretariat staff.

sentences.zh: 天監初，制度雖革，而日不暇給，嶸乃言曰：「永元肇亂，坐弄天爵，勳非卽戎，官以賄就。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian, though institutions were reformed, there was no leisure day by day; Rong then said: "When Yongyuan's turmoil began, men seized celestial rank while sitting idle; their merit did not come from taking up arms, and office came through bribery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianjian, though institutions changed, days allowed no rest; Rong said: "When Yongyuan's chaos began, men took heaven's ranks while sitting idle; merit came not from war, office from bribes.

sentences.zh: 揮一金而取九列，寄片札以招六校；

translations.literal: Waving one gold piece they took nine ranks; sending a brief note they recruited six colonels;
translations.idiomatic: One gold piece bought nine ranks; one slip of paper summoned six colonels;

sentences.zh: 騎都塞市，郎將填街。

translations.literal: Commandants of Horse filled the market, Generals of the Gentlemen packed the streets.
translations.idiomatic: Horse commandants clogged the markets and gentleman-generals the streets.

sentences.zh: 服旣纓組，尚爲臧獲之事；

translations.literal: Though wearing robes and ribbons, they still did servants' work;
translations.idiomatic: Robed and ribboned, they still did bondsmen's tasks;

sentences.zh: 職唯黃散，猶躬胥徒之役。

translations.literal: though office was only Cadet or Attendant, they still personally performed runners' chores.
translations.idiomatic: though posts were only yellow-gate cadets, they still ran errands themselves.

sentences.zh: 名實淆紊，茲焉莫甚。

translations.literal: Name and reality were tangled—nothing worse than this.
translations.idiomatic: Names and facts were confused—nothing worse.

sentences.zh: 臣愚謂軍官是素族士人，自有清貫，而因斯受爵，一宜削除，以懲僥競。

translations.literal: This servant is of the opinion that military officers who are of plain gentry families have their own clear pedigree, yet by this path receive noble ranks; such rewards should be erased in one stroke, to punish reckless rivalry.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that military officers of plain gentry have their own pedigree and should not gain rank this way—all such rewards should be cut off to check reckless competition.

sentences.zh: 若吏姓寒人，聽極其門品，不當因軍，遂濫清級。

translations.literal: If they are subordinate clerks of cold households, let them reach the utmost of their clan standing but they should not, because of military service, overflow into the clear grades.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks of poor houses may reach their clan's limit but must not, through army service, flood the clear grades.

sentences.zh: 若僑雜傖楚，應在綏撫，正宜嚴斷祿力，絕其妨正，直乞虛號而已。

translations.literal: If they are migrant mixed barbarians from Chu, they should be soothed and settled; one should simply cut off salaries and levies strictly, end their obstructing proper rule, and grant empty titles only.
translations.idiomatic: Migrant Chu riffraff should be soothed: cut salaries and levies, stop their harming government, and grant empty titles only.

sentences.zh: 謹竭愚忠，不恤衆口。

translations.literal: I present my foolish loyalty fully, heedless of the many mouths.
translations.idiomatic: I offer this loyal counsel, heedless of the crowd.

sentences.zh: 」敕付尚書行之。

translations.literal: " The edict was handed to the Ministry of Personnel to execute.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict was sent to the Ministry of Personnel to carry out.

sentences.zh: 遷中軍臨川王行參軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Staff Officer on the Central Army under the Prince of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He became staff officer on Prince Linchuan's central army.

sentences.zh: 衡陽王元簡出守會稽，引爲寧朔記室，專掌文翰。

translations.literal: When Prince of Hengyang Yuan Jian went out to guard Kuaiji, Rong was summoned as Record for Pacifying the North, solely in charge of literary records.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Hengyang Yuan Jian guarded Kuaiji, Rong became his Pacifying-the-North recorder, in sole charge of documents.

sentences.zh: 時居士何胤築室若邪山，山發洪水，漂拔樹石，此室獨存。

translations.literal: At the time the lay Buddhist He Yin built a house on Mt Ruoye; a flood burst from the mountain and swept away trees and stone, yet this dwelling alone remained.
translations.idiomatic: Layman He Yin built on Mt Ruoye; a mountain flood swept trees and stone away, yet his house alone stood.

sentences.zh: 元簡命嶸作《瑞室頌》以旌表之，辭甚典麗，選西中郎晉安王記室。

translations.literal: Yuan Jian ordered Rong to compose "Ode on the Auspicious Chamber" to proclaim it; the diction was very classical and fine. He was selected as Record of the Western Army under Prince Jin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jian had Rong write "Ode on the Auspicious Chamber" to honor it—very classical. He was chosen recorder to Prince Jin'an of the Western Army.

sentences.zh: 嶸嘗品古今五言詩，論其優劣，名爲《詩評》。

translations.literal: Rong once graded ancient and modern five-character poetry, discussing their merits, and entitled it *Critique of Poetry*.
translations.idiomatic: Rong once ranked ancient and modern five-character verse and titled the work *Critique of Poetry*.

sentences.zh: 其序曰：

translations.literal: Its preface says:
translations.idiomatic: Its preface reads:

sentences.zh: 氣之動物，物之感人，故搖盪性情，形諸舞詠。

translations.literal: When qi stirs things, things move people; thus feelings sway and take shape in dance and song.
translations.idiomatic: Qi moves things; things move people—so feeling stirs and finds form in dance and song.

sentences.zh: 欲以照燭三才，輝麗萬有，靈祇待之以致饗，幽微藉之以昭告。

translations.literal: It means to illuminate the three realms and shed glory on the myriad beings; spirits await it for offerings, and the hidden and subtle rely on it for proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: It lights the three powers and adorns the myriad; spirits wait on it for sacrifice, the hidden use it to declare.

sentences.zh: 動天地，感鬼神，莫近於詩。

translations.literal: Moving Heaven and Earth, touching spirits and ghosts—nothing comes nearer than poetry.
translations.idiomatic: To move Heaven and Earth and touch gods and ghosts, nothing nears poetry.

sentences.zh: 昔《南風》之辭，《卿雲》之頌，厥義夐矣。

translations.literal: Of old the words of the *Southern Winds* and the hymn *Cloud-Coach*—their meaning was already far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Of old *Southern Winds* and *Cloud-Coach*—their meaning was already vast.

sentences.zh: 《夏歌》曰「郁陶乎予心」，楚謠云「名余曰正則」，雖詩體未全，然略是五言之濫觴也。

translations.literal: The *Xia Songs* say "I am deeply troubled in heart"; a Chu song says "They named me Zhengze"—though the poetic form was not yet complete, they were roughly the source of five-character verse.
translations.idiomatic: *Xia Songs* have "deeply troubled in heart"; Chu songs name "Zhengze"—verse form was incomplete, yet these were the springs of five-character poetry.

sentences.zh: 逮漢李陵，始著五言之目。

translations.literal: Down to Han's Li Ling, the category of five-character verse was first set forth.
translations.idiomatic: By Han, Li Ling first established five-character verse as a category.

sentences.zh: 古詩眇邈，人代難詳，推其文體，固是炎漢之制，非衰周之倡也。

translations.literal: Ancient poems are remote and ages hard to trace; judging their form, they are truly products of blazing Han, not songs of declining Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient poems are distant and ages obscure; by form they belong to Han, not late Zhou.

sentences.zh: 自王、揚、枚、馬之徒，辭賦競爽，而吟詠靡聞。

translations.literal: From Wang, Yang, Mei, and Ma onward, rhapsodies vied in brilliance, yet lyric singing was scarcely heard.
translations.idiomatic: From Wang Bao, Yang Xiong, Mei Cheng, and Sima Xiangru on, fu competed in brilliance while lyric verse was rarely heard.

sentences.zh: 從李都尉訖班婕妤，將百年間，有婦人焉，一人而已。

translations.literal: From Commandant Li to Lady Ban, in nearly a hundred years there was a woman—and only one.
translations.idiomatic: From Li Ling to Lady Ban, nearly a century held one woman poet—and only one.

sentences.zh: 詩人之風，頓已缺喪。

translations.literal: The poets' tradition had suddenly perished.
translations.idiomatic: The poets' wind had suddenly died away.

sentences.zh: 東京二百載中，唯有班固《詠史》，質木無文致。

translations.literal: In the two hundred years of Eastern Han there was only Ban Gu's *Ode on History*—plain wood without literary grace.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Han's two centuries held only Ban Gu's *Ode on History*—plain and without literary grace.

sentences.zh: 降及建安，曹公父子，篤好斯文；

translations.literal: Down to the Jian'an period, Lord Cao and his sons deeply loved this craft;
translations.idiomatic: By Jian'an, the Cao lord and his sons deeply loved letters;

sentences.zh: 平原兄弟，鬱爲文棟；

translations.literal: the brothers of Pingyuan flourished as literary pillars;
translations.idiomatic: the Pingyuan brothers rose as literary pillars;

sentences.zh: 劉楨、王粲，爲其羽冀。

translations.literal: Liu Zhen and Wang Can were their wings.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhen and Wang Can were their wings.

sentences.zh: 次有攀龍託鳳，自致於屬車者，蓋將百計。

translations.literal: Next came those who, clinging to dragons and nesting phoenixes, attached themselves to the rear train—nearly a hundred in number.
translations.idiomatic: Next came nearly a hundred who clung to dragons and phoenixes and joined the train.

sentences.zh: 彬彬之盛，大備於時矣！

translations.literal: Such abundant flourishing was fully prepared in that age!
translations.idiomatic: Such abundant flowering was complete in that age!

sentences.zh: 爾後陵遲衰微，訖於有晉。

translations.literal: Afterward it declined and weakened, down to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward it declined to Jin.

sentences.zh: 太康中，三張二陸，兩潘一左，勃爾復興，踵武前王，風流未沫，亦文章之中興也。

translations.literal: In the Taikang era the three Zhangs, two Lus, two Pans, and one Zuo suddenly flourished again, following the martial ways of former kings; the breeze had not yet dried—this too was a literary revival.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang saw the three Zhangs, two Lus, two Pans, and Zuo Zuo revive the art—wind not yet spent, a literary revival.

sentences.zh: 永嘉時，貴黃、老，尚虛談，于時篇什，理過其辭，淡乎寡味。

translations.literal: In the Yongjia era Yellow Lao and empty talk were honored; poems of the time reasoned beyond their words and were thin and tasteless.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjia honored Huang-Lao and pure talk; verse reasoned past its words—thin and flavorless.

sentences.zh: 爰及江表，微波尚傳，孫綽、許詢、桓、庾諸公，皆平典似《道德論》，建安之風盡矣。

translations.literal: Reaching the lands south of the Yangtze, slight ripples still passed on; Sun Chuo, Xu Xun, Huan, Yu, and the gentlemen were all level and canonical like the *Dao De Lun*—Jian'an's wind was wholly gone.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river slight ripples remained; Sun Chuo, Xu Xun, Huan, and Yu wrote level pieces like the *Dao De Lun*—Jian'an's wind was gone.

sentences.zh: 先是郭景純用俊上之才，創變其體；

translations.literal: Earlier Guo Pu, with lofty talent, innovated and changed the form;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Guo Jingchun, with lofty talent, changed the form;

sentences.zh: 劉越石仗清剛之氣，贊成厥美。

translations.literal: Liu Kun, relying on pure firmness, helped perfect that beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yueshi, with pure firm spirit, helped perfect that beauty.

sentences.zh: 然彼衆我寡，未能動俗。

translations.literal: Yet they were many against few and could not move custom.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the many outweighed the few and could not shift custom.

sentences.zh: 逮義熙中，謝益壽斐然繼作；

translations.literal: By the Yixi era Xie Lingyun flourished and continued the work;
translations.idiomatic: By Yixi Xie Lingyun flourished and continued writing;

sentences.zh: 元嘉初，有謝靈運，才高辭盛，富豔難蹤，固已含跨劉、郭，陵轢潘、左。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia there was Xie Lingyun—talent high, diction rich, splendor hard to track; he already spanned Liu and Guo and towered over Pan and Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: Early Yuanjia brought Xie Lingyun—great talent, rich diction, splendor hard to follow; he spanned Liu and Guo and towered over Pan and Zuo.

sentences.zh: 故知陳思爲建安之傑，公幹、仲宣爲輔；

translations.literal: Thus we know Prince Si was Jian'an's paragon, with Gonggan and Zhongxuan as aides;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Prince Si was Jian'an's crown, Gonggan and Zhongxuan his aides;

sentences.zh: 陸機爲太康之英，安仁、景陽爲輔；

translations.literal: Lu Ji was Taikang's hero, with Anren and Jingyang as aides;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji was Taikang's hero, Anren and Jingyang his aides;

sentences.zh: 謝客爲元嘉之雄，顏延年爲輔：此皆五言之冠冕，文辭之命世。

translations.literal: Guest Xie was Yuanjia's champion, with Yan Yannian as aide: these are the crowns of five-character verse, fated masters of letters.
translations.idiomatic: Guest Xie was Yuanjia's champion, Yan Yannian his aide—these crown five-character verse and master an age of letters.

sentences.zh: 夫四言文約意廣，取效《風》、《騷》，便可多得，每苦文煩而意少，故世罕習焉。

translations.literal: Four-character writing is brief in words and broad in meaning; taking effect from the *Airs* and *Elegies*, one could get much, yet each suffers from many words and little meaning—hence the age rarely practices it.
translations.idiomatic: Four-character verse is brief and broad, modeled on *Airs* and *Elegies*, yet words crowd and meaning thins—so the age rarely uses it.

sentences.zh: 五言居文辭之要，是衆作之有滋味者也，故云會於流俗。

translations.literal: Five-character verse occupies the key place in letters; it is what gives flavor among all compositions—thus it is said to meet the flowing custom.
translations.idiomatic: Five-character verse holds the key in letters—it flavors all writing and meets the popular current.

sentences.zh: 豈不以指事遣形，窮情寫物，最爲詳切者邪！

translations.literal: Is it not because pointing at things and releasing form, exhausting feeling and writing things, is what is most detailed and apt!
translations.idiomatic: Does it not point at things, release form, exhaust feeling, and depict objects most closely!

sentences.zh: 故《詩》有六義焉，一曰興，二曰賦，三曰比。

translations.literal: Thus the *Odes* have six meanings: first xing, second fu, third bi.
translations.idiomatic: The *Odes* have six meanings: xing, fu, and bi.

sentences.zh: 文已盡而意有餘，興也；

translations.literal: When words are exhausted yet meaning remains—that is xing;
translations.idiomatic: Words end yet meaning lingers—that is xing;

sentences.zh: 因物喻志，比也；

translations.literal: using things to symbolize intent—that is bi;
translations.idiomatic: using things to symbolize intent—that is bi;

sentences.zh: 直書其事，寓言寫物，賦也。

translations.literal: directly stating the matter and entrusting words to depict things—that is fu.
translations.idiomatic: stating the matter directly and entrusting words to things—that is fu.

sentences.zh: 弘斯三義，酌而用之，幹之以風力，潤之以丹采，使味之者無極，聞之者動心，是詩之至也。

translations.literal: Expanding these three meanings and deploying them with measure, stiffening them with wind-strength and moistening them with cinnabar color, so that those who taste them find no limit and those who hear are moved in heart—that is poetry's utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Deploy the three with measure, stiffen with wind-power, moisten with color, so tasters find no end and hearers are moved—that is poetry's height.

sentences.zh: 若專用比、興，則患在意深，意深則辭躓。

translations.literal: If one uses only bi and xing, the trouble is meaning too deep; when meaning is deep, words stumble.
translations.idiomatic: Bi and xing alone make meaning too deep; deep meaning makes words stumble.

sentences.zh: 若但用賦體，則患在意浮，意浮則文散。

translations.literal: If one uses only the fu form, the trouble is meaning too floating; when meaning floats, writing scatters.
translations.idiomatic: Fu alone makes meaning too light; light meaning scatters the text.

sentences.zh: 嬉成流移，文無止泊，有蕪漫之累矣。

translations.literal: Play becomes drift; writing has no mooring—there is the flaw of rank luxuriance.
translations.idiomatic: Play becomes drift; writing lacks mooring—rank luxuriance follows.

sentences.zh: 若乃春風春鳥，秋月秋蟬，夏雲暑雨，冬月祁寒，斯四候之感諸詩者也。

translations.literal: Spring wind and spring birds, autumn moon and autumn insects, summer clouds and summer rain, winter moon and severe cold—these are the four seasons' impressions in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Spring birds, autumn insects, summer rain, winter cold—the four seasons' impressions in verse.

sentences.zh: 嘉會寄詩以親，離羣托詩以怨。

translations.literal: Festive gatherings lodge feeling in verse to draw kin near; parting from the group entrusts verse to voice grievance.
translations.idiomatic: Feasts lodge feeling in verse for kinship; parting entrusts verse for grievance.

sentences.zh: 至於楚臣去境，漢妾辭宮；

translations.literal: As for Chu ministers leaving their borders, Han concubines leaving the palace;
translations.idiomatic: Chu ministers leave their land; Han palace women leave the court;

sentences.zh: 或骨橫朔野，或魂逐飛蓬；

translations.literal: or bones lie across the northern wilds, or souls chase flying thistle;
translations.idiomatic: bones lie on northern wastes; souls chase thistle down;

sentences.zh: 或負戈外戍，或殺氣雄邊；

translations.literal: or they shoulder spears on distant garrison, or killing air swells on the frontier;
translations.idiomatic: they shoulder spears on distant guard; killing air swells on the border;

sentences.zh: 塞客衣單，霜閨淚盡。

translations.literal: frontier guests' coats are thin, frost chambers' tears are spent.
translations.idiomatic: frontier guests' coats are thin; frost chambers' tears are spent.

sentences.zh: 又士有解佩出朝，一去忘反；

translations.literal: Again, gentlemen unfasten their girdle pendants and leave court, going away and not returning;
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen unfasten pendants and leave court, never to return;

sentences.zh: 女有揚蛾入寵，再盼傾國。

translations.literal: women raise moth brows and enter favor, a second glance overturning the state.
translations.idiomatic: women raise moth brows and win favor; a second glance overturns a realm.

sentences.zh: 凡斯種種，感蕩心靈，非陳詩何以展其義，非長歌何以釋其情？

translations.literal: All such kinds stir and shake the heart—without presenting them in verse how could meaning be displayed, without long song how could feeling be released?
translations.idiomatic: All such stir the heart—without verse how show meaning, without long song how release feeling?

sentences.zh: 故曰：「《詩》可以羣，可以怨。

translations.literal: Thus it is said: "The *Odes* can unite, can voice grievance."
translations.idiomatic: Thus: "The *Odes* unite and voice grievance."

sentences.zh: 」使窮賤易安，幽居靡悶，莫尚於詩矣。

translations.literal: They make poverty easy to bear and seclusion free of gloom—nothing surpasses poetry.
translations.idiomatic: They ease poverty and lighten seclusion—nothing surpasses poetry.

sentences.zh: 故辭人作者，罔不愛好。

translations.literal: Thus writers of words have none who do not love it.
translations.idiomatic: Writers of words all love it.

sentences.zh: 今之士俗，斯風熾矣。

translations.literal: Among gentlemen and commoners today this wind blazes.
translations.idiomatic: Today gentry and commoners fan this wind hotly.

sentences.zh: 裁能勝衣，甫就小學，必甘心而馳騖焉。

translations.literal: Barely able to don clothes, just finished primary school, they must gladly gallop in it.
translations.idiomatic: Barely clothed, just out of primary school, they gallop in it gladly.

sentences.zh: 於是庸音雜體，各爲家法。

translations.literal: Then mediocre tones and mixed forms each become a family style.
translations.idiomatic: Mediocre tones and mixed forms each become a school.

sentences.zh: 至於膏腴子弟，恥文不逮，終朝點綴，分夜呻吟，獨觀謂爲警策，衆視終淪平鈍。

translations.literal: As for pampered sons ashamed their writing does not reach others, they embellish all day and groan through the night, alone deeming their work striking strategy while the crowd in the end sinks it to flat dullness.
translations.idiomatic: Pampered sons, shamed their writing falls short, polish all day and groan all night—alone they call it brilliant; the crowd finds it flat.

sentences.zh: 次有輕蕩之徒，笑曹、劉爲古拙，謂鮑昭羲皇上人，謝朓今古獨步；

translations.literal: Next are frivolous fellows who laugh at Cao and Liu as crude antiquity, call Bao Zhao a man above Fuxi, and Xie Tiao alone pacing past and present;
translations.idiomatic: Next come frivolous men who mock Cao and Liu as crude, call Bao Zhao above Fuxi, and Xie Tiao alone pacing all time;

sentences.zh: 而師鮑昭終不及「日中市朝滿」，學謝朓劣得「黃鳥度青枝」。

translations.literal: yet studying Bao Zhao they never reach "At noon the market is full," studying Xie Tiao they only manage "Yellow birds cross green branches."
translations.idiomatic: studying Bao they never reach "At noon the market fills"; studying Xie they only get "Yellow birds cross green boughs."

sentences.zh: 徒自棄於高聽，無涉於文流矣。

translations.literal: They cast themselves away from lofty hearing and have no part in the stream of letters.
translations.idiomatic: They abandon refined hearing and never join the current of letters.

sentences.zh: 嶸觀王公搢紳之士，每博論之餘，何嘗不以詩爲口實，隨其嗜欲，商榷不同。

translations.literal: Rong observed that among princes and gentry, whenever they broadly discussed, they never failed to make poetry their topic; following their appetites, appraisals differed.
translations.idiomatic: Rong saw that princes and gentry, in broad talk, always made poetry their topic; tastes differed in judgment.

sentences.zh: 淄澠並泛，朱紫相奪，喧嘩競起，准的無依。

translations.literal: Zi and Ying flowed together, vermilion and purple wrested each other; clamor rose in rivalry and there was no mark to aim at.
translations.idiomatic: Zi and Ying mingled, red and purple clashed; clamor rose with no mark to aim at.

sentences.zh: 近彭城劉士章，俊賞之士，疾其淆亂，欲爲當世詩品，口陳標榜，其文未遂，嶸感而作焉。

translations.literal: Recently Liu Shizhang of Pengcheng, a man of keen appreciation, hated this confusion and wished to make a contemporary *Grade of Poetry*; he orally set labels but his text was not completed—Rong, moved, composed it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shizhang of Pengcheng, keen in taste, hated the confusion and wished to grade contemporary verse orally but never finished—Rong, moved, wrote it.

sentences.zh: 昔九品論人，《七略》裁士，校以賓實，誠多未值；

translations.literal: Of old the nine ranks judged men and the *Seven Summaries* cut scholars, comparing substance to show much was missed;
translations.idiomatic: Nine ranks judged men and the *Seven Summaries* cut scholars—comparing substance, much was missed;

sentences.zh: 至若詩之爲技，較爾可知，以類推之，殆同博弈。

translations.literal: but as for poetry as a craft, comparison makes it fairly knowable; pushing by category, it is nearly like chess.
translations.idiomatic: poetry as craft is fairly known by comparison; by category it is like chess.

sentences.zh: 方今皇帝資生知之上才，體沈鬱之幽思，文麗日月，學究天人，昔在貴遊，已爲稱首；

translations.literal: Now the Emperor possesses talent born with knowledge above, embodies deep and brooding thought, his writing rivals sun and moon, his learning exhausts Heaven and man; of old among the nobility he was already chief in name;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor has inborn genius, deep brooding thought, writing that rivals sun and moon, learning that exhausts Heaven and man; among the nobility he was already foremost;

sentences.zh: 況八紘旣掩，風靡雲蒸，抱玉者連肩，握珠者踵武。

translations.literal: how much more when the eight directions are covered and wind rises like clouds—those embracing jade shoulder to shoulder, those grasping pearls tread in succession.
translations.idiomatic: now the realm is covered, wind and cloud rise; jade-bearers shoulder to shoulder, pearl-graspers follow in step.

sentences.zh: 固以睨漢、魏而弗顧，吞晉、宋於胸中。

translations.literal: He surely glances at Han and Wei without looking back and swallows Jin and Song in his breast.
translations.idiomatic: He glances past Han and Wei and holds Jin and Song in his breast.

sentences.zh: 諒非農歌轅議，敢致流別。

translations.literal: Truly this is not farm songs or carriage counsel—I dare bring flowing distinctions.
translations.idiomatic: This is no farm song or carriage debate—I dare only sort flowing ranks.

sentences.zh: 嶸之今錄，庶周遊於閭里，均之於談笑耳。

translations.literal: What Rong records now is only that you may wander the lanes and balance it in talk.
translations.idiomatic: What Rong records now is only for wandering lanes and balancing in talk.

sentences.zh: 頃之，卒官。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he died in office.

sentences.zh: 岏，字長岳，官至府參軍、建康平。

translations.literal: Wan, styled Changyue, reached office as staff officer and Jiankang magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Wan, styled Changyue, became staff officer and Jiankang magistrate.

sentences.zh: 著《良吏傳》十卷。

translations.literal: He authored *Biographies of Good Officials* in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote *Biographies of Good Officials* in ten juan.

sentences.zh: 嶼字季望，永嘉郡丞。

translations.literal: Yu, styled Jiwang, was Assistant Administrator of Yongjia commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, styled Jiwang, was Yongjia assistant administrator.

sentences.zh: 天監十五年，敕學士撰《徧略》，嶼亦預焉。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianjian an edict had scholars compile the *Comprehensive Digest*, and Yu also took part.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjian year fifteen ordered scholars to compile the *Comprehensive Digest*; Yu took part.

sentences.zh: 兄弟並有文集。

translations.literal: The brothers all had collected works.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers all had literary collections.

sentences.zh: 周興嗣字思纂，陳郡項人，漢太子太傅堪後也。

translations.literal: Zhou Xingsi, styled Sizuan, was a man of Xiang in Chen commandery, descendant of Han Heir Apparent Grand Tutor Zhou Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xingsi, styled Sizuan, was from Xiang in Chen, descendant of Han Heir Apparent Grand Tutor Zhou Kan.

sentences.zh: 高祖凝，晉征西府參軍、宜都太守。

translations.literal: His ancestor Ning served Jin as Staff Officer on the Western Campaign Headquarters and Grand Administrator of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestor Ning was Jin western-campaign staff officer and Yidu grand administrator.

sentences.zh: 興嗣世居姑孰。

translations.literal: The Xingsi family for generations lived at Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: The Xingsi clan lived at Gushu for generations.

sentences.zh: 年十三，遊學京師，積十餘載，遂博通記傳，善屬文。
