translations.literal: At thirteen he traveled to study in the capital; over more than ten years he came to master records broadly and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he studied in the capital; after ten-plus years he mastered records and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 嘗步自姑孰，投宿逆旅，夜有人謂之曰：「子才學邁世，初當見識貴臣，卒被知英主。

translations.literal: Once walking from Gushu he lodged at an inn; at night someone said to him: "Sir, your learning surpasses the age; at first you will be known to eminent ministers, and in the end favored by an outstanding lord."
translations.idiomatic: Walking from Gushu he lodged at an inn; at night a voice said: "Your learning surpasses the age; first eminent ministers will know you, then an outstanding lord."

sentences.zh: 」言終，不測所之。

translations.literal: When the speech ended, he could not tell where the man went.
translations.idiomatic: When it ended he could not tell where the man went.

sentences.zh: 齊隆昌中，侍中謝朏爲吳興太守，唯與興嗣談文史而已。

translations.literal: In Qi's Longchang era Attendant-in-ordinary Xie Tiao was Grand Administrator of Wuxing and discussed literature and history with Xingsi alone.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi's Longchang, Xie Tiao as Wuxing grand administrator discussed only literature and history with Xingsi.

sentences.zh: 及罷郡還，因大相稱薦。

translations.literal: When he left his post and returned, he greatly commended and recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving office he greatly praised and recommended him.

sentences.zh: 本州舉秀才，除桂陽郡丞，太守王嶸素相賞好，禮之甚厚。

translations.literal: The commandery recommended him as Outstanding Talent; he was appointed Assistant Administrator of Guiyang. Grand Administrator Wang Rong had long admired him and treated him with very thick courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as Outstanding Talent, he became Guiyang assistant; Grand Administrator Wang Rong long admired him and treated him generously.

sentences.zh: 高祖革命，興嗣奏《休平賦》，其文甚美，高祖嘉之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu overthrew the old regime, Xingsi submitted "Ode on Rest and Peace"; its writing was very fine and Gaozu praised it.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took power, Xingsi submitted "Ode on Rest and Peace"—very fine, and Gaozu praised it.

sentences.zh: 拜安成王國侍郎，直華林省。

translations.literal: He was appointed Gentleman of the Prince of Ancheng's state and served straight at the Hualin Office.
translations.idiomatic: He became Prince Ancheng's gentleman and served straight at Hualin.

sentences.zh: 其年，河南獻儛馬，詔興嗣與待詔到沆、張率爲賦，高祖以興嗣爲工。

translations.literal: That year Henan presented tribute horses; an edict had Xingsi and Attendant-at-Draft Dao Hong and Zhang Shuai compose fu; Gaozu regarded Xingsi's as best.
translations.idiomatic: That year Henan sent tribute horses; Gaozu had Xingsi, Dao Hong, and Zhang Shuai compose fu and judged Xingsi best.

sentences.zh: 擢員外散騎侍郎，進直文德、壽光省。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Cadet-Attendant Emeritus and advanced to serve straight in the Wende and Shouguang offices.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to cadet-attendant emeritus and served straight in Wende and Shouguang.

sentences.zh: 是時，高祖以三橋舊宅爲光宅寺，敕興嗣與陸倕各制寺碑。

translations.literal: At that time Gaozu made the old residence at Three Bridges into Guangzai Temple and ordered Xingsi and Lu Yan each to compose a temple stele.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu made the Three Bridges old residence Guangzai Temple and ordered Xingsi and Lu Yan each to write a stele.

sentences.zh: 及成俱奏，高祖用興嗣所制者。

translations.literal: When both were submitted Gaozu used the one Xingsi composed.
translations.idiomatic: Both were submitted; Gaozu used Xingsi's.

sentences.zh: 自是《銅表銘》、《柵塘碣》、《北伐檄》、《次韻王羲之書千字》，並使興嗣爲文；

translations.literal: From then on the Bronze Column Inscription, Barrier Pond Stele, Northern Expedition Proclamation, and verse matching Wang Xizhi's Thousand Characters were all entrusted to Xingsi for the text;
translations.idiomatic: Thence the bronze-column inscription, barrier-pond stele, northern expedition proclamation, and verse matching Wang Xizhi's Thousand Characters all went to Xingsi;

sentences.zh: 每奏，高祖輒稱善，加賜金帛。

translations.literal: each time he submitted, Gaozu would praise it and add gifts of gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: each submission won praise and gifts of gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 九年，除新安郡丞，秩滿，復爲員外散騎侍郎，佐撰國史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Assistant Administrator of Xin'an; when his term expired he again became Cadet-Attendant Emeritus and assisted in compiling the National History.
translations.idiomatic: Year nine he became Xin'an assistant; after his term he again became cadet-attendant emeritus and helped compile national history.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遷給事中，撰文如故。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to Supervisor of Attendants, composing documents as before.
translations.idiomatic: Year twelve he became supervisor of attendants, writing as before.

sentences.zh: 興嗣兩手先患風疽，是年又染癘疾，左目盲，高祖撫其手，嗟曰：「斯人也而有斯疾也！

translations.literal: Xingsi had long suffered wind sores in both hands; that year he also caught plague, his left eye went blind; Gaozu stroked his hand and sighed: "That a man like this should have such an illness!"
translations.idiomatic: Xingsi long had wind sores in both hands; that year plague came and his left eye went blind; Gaozu stroked his hand: "That such a man should have such illness!"

sentences.zh: 」手疏治疽方以賜之。

translations.literal: By hand he drafted a prescription for treating sores and bestowed it on him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu drafted a sore-treatment prescription by hand and gave it him.

sentences.zh: 其見惜如此。

translations.literal: He was cherished thus.
translations.idiomatic: He was cherished thus.

sentences.zh: 任昉又愛其才，常言曰：「周興嗣若無疾，旬日當至御史中丞。

translations.literal: Ren Fang also loved his talent and often said: "Were it not for Zhou Xingsi's illness, within ten days he would reach Vice Director of the Secretariat Censorate."
translations.idiomatic: Ren Fang loved his talent and said: "Without Zhou Xingsi's illness, within ten days he would reach vice censor-in-chief."

sentences.zh: 」十四年，除臨川郡丞。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Assistant Administrator of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Year fourteen he became Linchuan assistant.

sentences.zh: 十七年，復爲給事中，直西省。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he again became Supervisor of Attendants, serving straight in the Western Office.
translations.idiomatic: Year seventeen he again became supervisor of attendants, serving straight in the Western Office.

sentences.zh: 左衛率周捨奉敕注高祖所制歷代賦，啓興嗣助焉。

translations.literal: Leader of the Left Guard Zhou She received an edict to annotate the various fu composed by successive emperors as ordered by Gaozu, and memorialized that Xingsi should assist.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou She of the Left Guard received an edict to annotate imperial fu and asked Xingsi to assist.

sentences.zh: 普通二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Putong he died.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong year two he died.

sentences.zh: 所撰《皇帝實錄》、《皇德記》、《起居注》、《職儀》等百餘卷，文集十卷。

translations.literal: What he compiled—*Imperial Veritable Records*, *Record of Imperial Virtue*, *Daily Records*, *Rites of Office*, and the like—totaled over a hundred juan, and his collected writings ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled *Imperial Veritable Records*, *Record of Imperial Virtue*, *Daily Records*, *Rites of Office*, and more—over a hundred juan—and ten juan of collected writings.

sentences.zh: 先是，有廣陵高爽、濟陽江洪、會稽虞騫，並工屬文。

translations.literal: Earlier there were Gao Shuang of Guangling, Jiang Hong of Jiyang, and Yu Qian of Kuaiji, all skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Gao Shuang of Guangling, Jiang Hong of Jiyang, and Yu Qian of Kuaiji all wrote well.

sentences.zh: 爽，齊永明中贈衛軍王儉詩，爲儉所賞，及領丹陽尹，舉爽郡孝廉。

translations.literal: Shuang, in Qi's Yongming era, presented a poem to Defender-General Wang Jian, was esteemed by Jian; when Jian headed Danyang as Governor he recommended Shuang as commandery Filial and Incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang in Yongming presented verse to Wang Jian, won his esteem, and when Jian governed Danyang recommended him as filial and incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 天監初，歷官中軍臨川王參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he served in succession as Staff Officer on the Central Army under the Prince of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tianjian he served as Prince Linchuan's central-army staff officer.

sentences.zh: 出爲晉陵令，坐事繫冶，作《鑊魚賦》以自況，其文甚工。

translations.literal: He went out as magistrate of Jinling; for an offense he was imprisoned in the foundry, composed "Rhapsody on the Cauldron-Fish" to depict his plight—the writing was very accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: As Jinling magistrate he was imprisoned in the foundry for an offense and wrote "Rhapsody on the Cauldron-Fish" to depict his plight—very accomplished.

sentences.zh: 後遇赦獲免，頃之，卒。

translations.literal: Later, meeting an amnesty he was released; not long after, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Later an amnesty freed him; soon after he died.

sentences.zh: 洪爲建陽令，坐事死。

translations.literal: Hong was magistrate of Jianyang and was executed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was Jianyang magistrate and was executed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 騫官至王國侍郎。

translations.literal: Qian rose to Gentleman of a princely state.
translations.idiomatic: Qian rose to a princely gentleman.

sentences.zh: 並有文集。

translations.literal: All had collected works.
translations.idiomatic: All had literary collections.
